lines.text: Okay, so... Le Chonk wanted to play. So we gave him DOOM.
Well, technically, it's Mistral Large 4 doing the playing. We built it a little DOOM-style shooter: three levels, keys, locked doors, a few explosive barrels... and Rex, the boss.
Here's the trick. Every turn, time just... stops. The model gets the screen, plus a short note: its health, a map, and the doors and items it's already seen.
See the ruler under the view? It turns "where's that mouse?" into something simple, like: turn left, twenty-five degrees.
Then it answers with one move: a thought, a few actions, and a note to itself. And time starts again. If it gets hurt, or spots a new enemy, it stops... and thinks again.
And yes, it talks the whole time, like a very dramatic French cat. These are its real thoughts.

So, how good is it? We put Mistral Large 4 up against other open models: Kwen, G L M, Kee-mee, Gemma, and DeepSeek. Same game, same rules. On their best runs, Large 4 comes out on top. And it costs about thirteen cents a level.
It's all TypeScript and three J S. The art, the music, the sounds... all made in code. And every single run can be replayed, frame by frame.
Want to try it? Play it yourself, or just sit back and watch Le Chonk play. The link's right below.
